learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with basic knowledge of spatial geometry.
Introduce the student to the use of scales, measurement systems, and representation systems.

syllabus_topics: Descriptive Geometry: Dihedral system, axonometric system, cavalier perspective system, contour plane system
Representation of the line. Traces. Visibility. Positions
The plane. Ways to define it. Traces. Lines and points in the plane
Characteristic lines of the plane. Positions
Exercises on representation of points, lines, and planes. Membership relations.
DIHEDRAL SYSTEM: INTERSECTIONS OF LINES AND/OR PLANES
DIHEDRAL SYSTEM: PARALLELISM, PERPENDICULARITY AND DISTANCES
Incidence of a line and plane sections
Auxiliary planes and types of intersection
Representation of the point, line, and plane. Slope, difference in level, module
Parallelism and perpendicularity. Intersections of planes
Applications: Terrain representation. Longitudinal and transverse profiles. Cuttings and embankments
teaching_methods: Personal study, individual or group work, and bibliography reading

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or cumulative and/or eliminatory partial exams
Resolution and delivery of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: Evaluation can be done through two options: Continuous Evaluation (Option 1) or Final Exam (Option 2). For Option 1, 80% of the grade comes from two non-recoverable continuous assessment activities (EC1, EC2) and 20% from recoverable academic works (NTA). The grade for continuous activities (NEC) must be greater than or equal to 5 for the final grade formula to apply; otherwise, the final grade is minimum{4, NF}. For Option 2, 80% of the grade comes from a recoverable final exam (NEF) and 20% from recoverable academic works (NTA). The NEF must be greater than or equal to 5 for the final grade formula to apply; otherwise, the final grade is minimum{4, NF}. Global Evaluation consists of a final exam (80% of grade from exercises EF1-EF5) and additional exercises (20% of grade from SDEX1-SDEX2); the final grade (NF) must be greater than or equal to 5.
